Merge a Named List of Seurat Objects into One

Source: R/mergeSeurat.R
mergeSeurat.Rd

Combines a named list of per-sample Seurat objects – typically the output of seuratFrom10x() – into a single object via merge(), prefixing every cell barcode with its sample name so barcodes stay unique and traceable back to their sample of origin.

Usage

mergeSeurat(objList, joinLayers = TRUE)

Arguments

objList

Named list of Seurat objects, one per sample, as returned by seuratFrom10x(). Names are used as cell barcode prefixes and must be unique.

joinLayers

Under Seurat 5, join the per-sample layers merge() creates back into one per kind of data. Defaults to TRUE. Ignored under Seurat 4, which never splits them. See Seurat 4 and Seurat 5.

Value

A single merged Seurat object, returned invisibly (the object is printed as a side effect). Cell barcodes are prefixed with their sample name; the Ident column is carried through from the inputs. If objList has exactly one element, that element is returned unmerged and unprefixed, with a message.

Details

The list names are load-bearing: they are passed to merge() as add.cell.id, so a cell AAACCCAAGA-1 in list entry Sample_1 becomes Sample_1_AAACCCAAGA-1 in the merged object. Names must therefore be present, non-blank and unique.

The whole list is validated up front, so a malformed batch fails with a specific message instead of partway through the merge. In order, objList must:

  • be non-empty (a single-element list short-circuits – see Value);

  • contain only structurally valid Seurat objects;

  • be fully named, with no NA, blank or duplicated names;

  • contain no zero-cell objects;

  • carry an Ident metadata column, which seuratFrom10x() sets to the sample name;

  • agree on Seurat::DefaultAssay() across every element.

Two further checks run after the merge, guarding against a merge that silently loses data: every sample must still be represented in the merged Ident metadata column, and the merged cell count must equal the sum of the inputs'.

Seurat 4 and Seurat 5

The installed version is detected automatically. Under Seurat 4, merge() binds every sample's counts into one matrix. Under Seurat 5 it keeps one layer per sample (counts.Sample_A, counts.Sample_B, ...), which is what Seurat 5's IntegrateLayers() wants but not what most other code expects. By default those layers are joined, so the merged object has the same shape whichever version made it. Set joinLayers = FALSE to keep them split; under Seurat 4 the argument has no effect.

See also

seuratFrom10x(), which produces the named list this expects.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
seurat_list <- seuratFrom10x(
  path        = "/path/to/Pool1/outs",
  multi = TRUE
)

merged <- mergeSeurat(seurat_list)

# barcodes are namespaced by sample
head(colnames(merged))

# and Ident still identifies the sample of origin
table(merged$Ident)
} # }
